sentences.text: Rothia dentocariosa is a Gram-positive actinobacterium counted as part of the physiological oral flora.
Isolates are catalase positive, reduce nitrate and nitrite, hydrolyse esculin and produce acid from glucose, sucrose, maltose, salicin and glycerol.
It is frequently isolated from human clinical material and must be differentiated from morphologically similar organisms of the genera Actinomyces and Nocardia.
Published case reports describe it as a rare cause of infective endocarditis, usually in patients with prior heart conditions, and studies have associated it with periodontal inflammatory disease.
